title: UEFA Euro 2012 squads — Grokipedia
content: The UEFA Euro 2012 squads comprised the 23-player rosters selected by each of the 16 national teams that competed in the 14th UEFA European Football Championship, co-hosted by Poland and Ukraine from 8 June to 1 July 2012.](#ref-1)](#ref-2) These squads were finalized by a 12:00 CET deadline on 29 May 2012, ten days before the tournament's opening match, in line with UEFA regulations that permitted alterations only for serious injuries verified by a UEFA Medical Committee doctor and the team's physician prior to each nation's first fixture.](#ref-1) The participating teams were divided into four groups: **Group A** (Czech Republic, Greece, Poland, Russia), **Group B** (Denmark, Germany, Netherlands, Portugal), **Group C** (Croatia, Republic of Ireland, Italy, Spain), and **Group D** (England, France, Sweden, Ukraine), with squads reflecting a balance of experienced stars and emerging talents qualified through UEFA's group and playoff stages.](#ref-1) Notable aspects of the squads included the dominance of club affiliations from top European leagues, such as Spain's roster heavily featuring players from Real Madrid and Barcelona, which contributed to their 4-0 final victory over Italy at Kyiv's Olympiyskiy Stadium.](#ref-2)](#ref-3) Injuries prompted last-minute changes, like Denmark replacing Thomas Sørensen with Kasper Schmeichel and Republic of Ireland substituting Paul McShane for injured players, underscoring the high-stakes preparation amid the tournament's expanded format since 1996.](#ref-1) The UEFA technical analysis later highlighted tactical diversity across squads, with an average match attendance of 46,471 spectators witnessing the blend of defensive solidity and attacking flair that defined the event.](#ref-4)](#ref-5).

title: UEFA Euro 2012 - Wikipedia
content: # UEFA Euro 2012. The **2012 UEFA European Football Championship**, commonly referred to as **UEFA Euro 2012** or simply **Euro 2012**, was the 14th European Championship for men's national football teams "List of men's national association football teams") organised by UEFA. The final tournament, held between 8 June and 1 July 2012, was co-hosted by Poland and Ukraine (both first time hosts), and was won by Spain, who beat Italy in the final at the Olympic Stadium, Kyiv, Ukraine. The two host teams qualified automatically while the remaining 14 finalists were decided through a qualifying competition, featuring 51 teams, from August 2010 to November 2011. This was the last European Championship to employ the 16-team finals format in use since 1996; from Euro 2016 onward, it was expanded to 24 finalists. Euro 2012 was played at eight venues, four in each host country. As at Euro 2008 in Austria and Switzerland, both 2012 host nations were eliminated in the group stage.
